question.text: For equity scheme purchases, the applicable NAV is the closing NAV of:

answer.text: The day on which the application form is submitted at the ISC
The next business day after application submission
The day on which the cheque is deposited by the investor
The day on which funds are available for utilisation by the AMC

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series II-B workbook (pp.141-142), for equity and debt scheme purchases and switch-ins, the applicable NAV is the closing NAV of the day on which the funds are available for utilisation by the AMC, irrespective of the time of receipt of the application. The Trap: The trigger is funds availability for utilisation — not the application submission time. A form submitted at 2 PM with funds that only become available the next business day will get the NAV of that later day, not the day the form was received. Note: Recommend online/RTGS transfers for NAV-sensitive purchases. Cheque-clearing delays can defer funds availability and push the applicable NAV to a later date, which can matter materially in volatile or rising markets.
